# Tasks: Function App to Container App Cutover

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/006-cutover/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, quickstart.md (all generated by `/speckit-plan`)

**Tests**: None. Per FR-008, verification is manual (DevTools Network tab, `curl -X OPTIONS`, `az functionapp show`). No Playwright, Postman, or CI test is added for this slice.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story, but **sequenced in the operational order from `quickstart.md` section A (FR-014)**: CORS deploy (US2 Bicep + deploy) → frontend swap (US1) → verify US1 end-to-end → verify US2 preflights → stop Function App (US3) LAST. The US priority labels are preserved for traceability.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] [OWNER?] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel with another `[P]` task (different file, no dependency on an incomplete task).
- **[Story]**: Which user story the task belongs to (US1, US2, US3).
- **[OWNER]**: Owner-only step — the operator runs it (merge, workflow watch, `az` CLI). Not an edit any agent can perform in a sandbox.
- Each task names the exact file or command.

## Path Conventions

- `movie-tracker-api/` (this repo): Bicep + Spec Kit artefacts.
- `movie-tracker-app/` (sibling repo, `C:\projects\dev\movie-tracker-app`): one frontend edit on `main`.

## Phase 3: User Story 2 — CORS parity set (Priority: P2) — step A.2

**Goal**: Replace the Container App ingress `corsPolicy.allowedOrigins` wildcard with the Function App's historical parity set so the frontend's production SWA origin and the Angular `ng serve` dev origin are the only allowed cross-origin callers.

**Independent Test**: After the Bicep deploys, `az containerapp show --name movie-tracker-api --resource-group RG-MovieTracker-Demo --query 'properties.configuration.ingress.corsPolicy.allowedOrigins'` returns exactly `['https://green-mud-037bbdc1e.5.azurestaticapps.net', 'http://localhost:4200']` with no `*`. Preflights from each parity origin echo that origin; preflights from any other origin do not.

**Why first operationally**: FR-014 fixes this ordering (CORS deploy first, frontend swap second, verification third, FA stop last).

### Implementation for User Story 2

- [X] T004 [US2] Edit `infrastructure/container-app.bicep`: change the ingress `corsPolicy.allowedOrigins` value from `['*']` to `[ 'https://green-mud-037bbdc1e.5.azurestaticapps.net', 'http://localhost:4200' ]` (preserve `allowedMethods`, `allowedHeaders`, `allowCredentials`, `maxAge` exactly as-is). Lines around `corsPolicy` begin at ~line 115 of the file.
- [X] T005 [US2] [OWNER] Before committing, confirm the staged diff of this slice is bounded to the two paths SC-005 names: `specs/006-cutover/**` and `infrastructure/container-app.bicep` only. `.gitignore`, `MovieTracker.Api/**`, and other `infrastructure/*.bicep` files are untouched. If any file outside those prefixes is staged, `git restore --staged <path>` to unstage it before T006. Operator-only because it may require git mutations.
- [ ] T006 [US2] [OWNER] Commit on `006-cutover` and push; open a PR. Watch the `Validate Bicep` and `What-If Analysis` jobs in `.github/workflows/infra-deploy.yml`. The intended What-If change is on `Microsoft.App/containerApps/movie-tracker-api`'s ingress `corsPolicy.allowedOrigins`. Any additional change is investigated and resolved before merge; a delete or replace blocks the merge (SC-006).
- [ ] T007 [US2] [OWNER] Merge the PR into `main`. The `Deploy Infrastructure` job in `.github/workflows/infra-deploy.yml` applies the change.
- [ ] T008 [US2] [OWNER] Verify the deployed value: run the `az containerapp show ... --query 'properties.configuration.ingress.corsPolicy.allowedOrigins'` command from `quickstart.md` section A.2 and confirm the two parity origins (no `*`).

**Checkpoint**: Container App ingress CORS is parity-tightened on the live environment. The verification preflights (US2's independent test) are deferred to Phase 5 to follow FR-014's verification order (US1 end-to-end check first, then US2 preflights).

## Phase 4: User Story 1 — Frontend chatBaseUrl swap + SWA redeploy (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP — steps A.3–A.4

**Goal**: Point the deployed Static Web App at the Container App by changing one `chatBaseUrl` constant in the frontend repo, letting the frontend's existing GitHub Actions workflow build, stage, E2E, and promote.

**Independent Test** (US1): After the SWA production deploy succeeds, open the production SWA URL with DevTools Network open, run one `start` + two `ask` exchanges, and confirm every chat request hits the Container App host and zero hit the Function App host.

### Implementation for User Story 1

- [ ] T009 [US1] [OWNER] In `C:\projects\dev\movie-tracker-app` on `main`, edit `src/enviroments/enviroments.ts`: change the `chatBaseUrl` value from `'https://yh5ax4ws5lr3k-func-movie-tracker.azurewebsites.net/api/chat'` to `'https://movie-tracker-api.politeocean-1c0085f8.westus3.azurecontainerapps.io/api/chat'`. Preserve the `/api/chat` suffix exactly. Leave every other property in the file unchanged. Do NOT touch `.claude/`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `copilot-instructions.md`, `movietracker-demo.mp4`, or `test-results/` (FR-013). Do NOT edit `.gitignore` (FR-007).
- [ ] T010 [US1] [OWNER] Commit the single-file change on `main` and push. The push fires `.github/workflows/azure-static-web-apps-green-mud-037bbdc1e.yml`: build with the new URL, deploy to staging slot, run the existing Playwright E2E against staging, promote to production on green. Do NOT edit the workflow or Playwright tests (FR-011). If staging E2E fails, STOP and surface the failure — do not patch tests to force green.
- [ ] T011 [US1] [OWNER] Watch `.github/workflows/azure-static-web-apps-green-mud-037bbdc1e.yml` in the Actions tab until the production deploy step reports success. Do NOT proceed to T012 before production is green; the deployed SWA bundle is what T012 verifies against.
- [ ] T012 [US1] [OWNER] Open the deployed production SWA (`https://green-mud-037bbdc1e.5.azurestaticapps.net`) in a browser with DevTools Network open and run the four verifications from `quickstart.md` section A.4: `start` request hits Container App host (200 + non-empty `chatId`), two `ask` exchanges on the same `chatId` hit the Container App host (200 + non-empty responses rendered), and zero requests target the Function App host. If any check fails, apply the rollback from `quickstart.md` section A.7.

**Checkpoint**: The deployed SWA is driving traffic to the Container App end-to-end. CORS has been live-tightened since Phase 3, so the browser's preflights are already passing against the parity set.

## Phase 5: User Story 2 continued — CORS preflight verification (Priority: P2) — step A.5

**Goal**: Prove the ingress CORS policy enforces the parity set with no wildcard, now that there is live traffic to confirm it does not break the real flow.

**Independent Test** (US2): Three `curl -X OPTIONS` preflights return the expected `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` behaviour (echo for parity origins, absent/non-matching for off-list origins).

### Implementation for User Story 2 (preflight checks)

- [ ] T013 [US2] [OWNER] Run the three `curl.exe -i -X OPTIONS` preflights from `quickstart.md` section A.5 (one with `Origin: https://green-mud-037bbdc1e.5.azurestaticapps.net`, one with `Origin: http://localhost:4200`, one with `Origin: https://evil.example.com`). Confirm the first two responses include `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <that exact origin>` and the third does not grant access to `evil.example.com`.
- [ ] T014 [US2] [OWNER] Re-run T012's verification (one full chat round-trip on the deployed SWA) to confirm the tightened policy did not break the real browser flow (FR-003 acceptance scenario 4).

**Checkpoint**: US1 (frontend→Container App end-to-end) and US2 (CORS parity, no wildcard, real flow still works) are both verified against the live stack. Phase 6 is unblocked.

## Phase 6: User Story 3 — Stop the Function App (Priority: P3) LAST — step A.6

**Goal**: Stop (not delete) the Function App `yh5ax4ws5lr3k-func-movie-tracker` so no stale caller can silently reach a parallel backend, after US1 and US2 verify green on the deployed stack.

**Independent Test** (US3): `az functionapp show --ids $functionAppId --query state` returns `"Stopped"` and a GET to the Function App's `/api/chat/start` URL no longer returns a `chatId`. The resource still exists in its resource group (not deleted).

**Why LAST** (FR-014): Stopping the Function App before the frontend verifies on the Container App would create an outage. The order is enforced: this phase does not start until T014 passes.

### Implementation for User Story 3

- [ ] T015 [US3] [OWNER] Resolve the Function App's hosting scope with `az graph query -q "Resources | where type == 'microsoft.web/sites' and name == 'yh5ax4ws5lr3k-func-movie-tracker' | project id, name, subscriptionId, resourceGroup, location" -o json`. Record the `id` (full resource ID). If the query returns zero rows, record "not visible under any accessible subscription" and surface to the slice owner — do NOT treat "not found" as "already stopped" (FR-005).
- [ ] T016 [US3] [OWNER] With the resolved `--ids $functionAppId`, run `az functionapp show --ids $functionAppId --query state`. If `"Running"`, run `az functionapp stop --ids $functionAppId` and re-check for `"Stopped"`. If already `"Stopped"`, record "already stopped" and skip the stop command (FR-005).
- [ ] T017 [US3] [OWNER] Confirm the old hostname no longer serves chat: `curl.exe -i https://yh5ax4ws5lr3k-func-movie-tracker.azurewebsites.net/api/chat/start` should return 403, 503, or a connection error — not a 200 with a `chatId`.
- [ ] T018 [US3] [OWNER] Re-run T012's end-to-end chat verification one last time on the deployed SWA to confirm chat still works (because it already targets the Container App). FR-006 preserves the resource: do NOT run `az functionapp delete`, `az resource delete`, or any portal delete.

**Checkpoint**: Function App is stopped and preserved. Cutover is complete. The SC-005 diff-scope check already ran at T005 before anything was committed.

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Phase 1 (Setup)**: No dependencies. Start immediately.
- **Phase 2 (Foundational)**: Empty. No gate.
- **Phase 3 (US2 CORS deploy)**: After Phase 1. Must land on the live Container App before Phase 4.
- **Phase 4 (US1 frontend swap)**: After Phase 3's T008 confirms the deployed CORS allowlist.
- **Phase 5 (US2 preflight checks)**: After Phase 4's T012 (chat works end-to-end).
- **Phase 6 (US3 FA stop)**: After Phase 5's T014. **This is the FR-014 "stop LAST" rule.**

### Within Each User Story

- In this repo (US2): the Bicep edit (T004) precedes the diff-scope check (T005), which precedes the commit/PR (T006), which precedes merge (T007), which precedes the deployed-value check (T008).
- In the frontend repo (US1): the TS edit (T009) precedes commit/push (T010), which precedes the workflow-watch gate (T011), which precedes the browser verification (T012).
- Deploy steps precede their verification steps; verification steps precede any downstream phase that depends on them.

### Parallel Opportunities

- None by design. The slice is a strictly ordered operational sequence; the `[P]` marker is intentionally absent across the whole plan.

---

## Owner-only tasks (summary)

Fifteen of eighteen tasks are `[OWNER]`: everything that mutates git state, merges, pushes, triggers a workflow, runs `az`, or inspects live Azure state. The three non-OWNER tasks are the quickstart presence check (T002), the no-touch verification (T003), and the Bicep file edit (T004) — those three an agent can safely perform in a sandbox; the rest require operator credentials and live-system access. (T001 and T005 are `[OWNER]` because they may mutate local git state.)

---

## Implementation Strategy

### Operational order is the strategy

This slice is not an MVP-first-then-polish feature; it is a cutover whose order is a hard requirement (FR-014). Execute Phase 3 → Phase 4 → Phase 5 → Phase 6, in that order, with each phase's checkpoint satisfied before the next starts. Rollback steps are in `quickstart.md` section A.7; the CORS parity set stays in place during any rollback (reverting to `['*']` is explicitly out of scope per FR-004).

### Pause points

- After Phase 3 T008: pause until the deployed CORS array shows the parity set.
- After Phase 4 T012: pause until the end-to-end chat flow is green on the deployed SWA.
- After Phase 5 T014: pause until all three preflight checks and the re-run chat check pass.
- Only then: Phase 6 (`az functionapp stop`).

---

## Notes

- `[P]` is unused — the whole slice is strictly serial by design.
- `[Story]` labels are present for traceability back to spec.md's three user stories (US1, US2, US3).
- `[OWNER]` labels mark tasks that require operator action (merge, push, workflow watch, `az` CLI, live-site browser verification).
- No new tests, no new config, no new tooling, no new npm scripts, no new environment files, no new DI, no new endpoints, no new CORS middleware. Spec FR-002 forbids all of these.
- The frontend edit (T009) is made in `C:\projects\dev\movie-tracker-app` on `main`, not in this repository. Its commit lives in the frontend repo; this slice documents the edit and the trigger for the SWA workflow.
